title: Run takeover
summary: Successor creation evaluates the older run through complete frozen QA selections. An incomplete historical selection refuses with reviewed operator repair recovery before resumption. Original source and target identities remain authoritative. A containing successor on the same flow and target takes over waiting members under existing QA and approval rules. The takeover settles the old run in the same transaction, moving its members through one batched removal and one batched admission so its cost does not grow with the member count. Without shared QA or approval, a member stays in the old run only when the old run already closed it; every unclosed member, including a passed-but-open, refused or non-final one, moves. The old run then reads succeeded when it delivered at least one member and cancelled when none stayed, so it never sits executing without a driver; a refused succeeded gate refuses the takeover with takeover_settlement_refused. With shared QA or approval every unclosed member moves and the old run is cancelled, so no approval is skipped. While a live steering seat covers the project only the seat holder or the older run's creating session may take it over, live driver or not; other sessions are refused with takeover_reserved_for_steering and report the landing to steering. start-for-item creates, takes over, enrolls and validates in one transaction, so any refusal writes nothing and an item the takeover moved is enrolled once. Unlocked creation prepares carried-work facts against the waiting run when takeover would settle it succeeded, projecting unclosed member movement in a transaction that rolls back without removal audits, notices or settlement; cancelled takeovers retain the preceding succeeded release as their base. Locked validation rechecks settlement against current state. Exhausted creation preparation names the original create or start-for-item command and idempotency key as recovery. The successor's carried work compares from the run it settled, each repository comparison counted on its own; a comparison the repository cannot answer records carried work as unknown with its named reason and recovery rather than failing creation, and the settled run's own carried work is recorded after creation commits. Creation refuses up front when the caller's machine could not drive a self-deploy run. A takeover that aborts no running QA execution sends the owner no notice. When it aborts one, the waking notice names the new run and says to keep the claim and stay parked. Takeover stays immediate but never frees a host that may be dirty: a moved member's execution whose runner checked in on a host case, or a mission walk holding its machine, keeps custody and heartbeat authority under the recorded cooperative abort, the old run's cancellation leaves that abort in place, and the lease releases only after restore proof or walk-end teardown, so no waiting execution is granted the host first; the notice then names that cleanup.
